about: The berth deck of the frigate Commonwealth as built, 1797 (docs/shipkit-13): the planked deck 7 ft 2 in under the gun deck, the side's ceiling up to the gun deck, the gun deck's beams over it, its hatchways, ladders and the fittings that come down through it (the capstan's spindle, the riding bitts' posts, the pumps' trees, the masts and the cables), the tiller room aft (where the iron tiller goes is still to be decided: tiller), the wardroom with its state rooms, the steerage and the officers' rooms forward of it, the crew's deck where the men slung their hammocks by night (about 110 here: berthing) and ate at mess tables by day, the sick bay forward, and the lanterns. Lengths in feet (_ft) and inches (_in) unless a key says metres (_m). Each value carries its source; 'estimate' means period practice or proportion, not a drawing. berthdeck.py reads this file; what it hands the orlop slice (14) is the build's berth_deck.json, written from the deck as built (handover)

sources.profile_1849: NARA 75841356, the inboard profile in the Navy Yard Boston set of 1849 (public domain; local copy in Data/Reference, measured only): the berth deck's bulkheads aft of the main mast (the wardroom with its state rooms either side, the steerage forward of it, the rooms forward of that) and the sick bay forward; read for the arrangement, the 1797 rooms placed between this ship's own beams (estimate)
sources.midship_1795: NARA 75841360, the midship section drawn from Humphreys' specifications, and the 1926 midship section (the orlop slice's reading): the deck 7 ft 2 in under the gun deck, its planks 3 1/2 in yellow pine, the gun deck's beams 15 by 18 in over it (berth_deck.json sources)
sources.museum_1812: the USS Constitution Museum's description of the ship in 1812: steered from the spar deck by a double wheel through tiller ropes to an iron tiller on the berth deck aft of the wardroom; the crew slept in hammocks on the berth deck, 14 in apart, and messed there
sources.period: estimate: period practice for an American or British frigate of the 1790s where neither drawing shows a part (the framing's sizes, the ceiling, the rooms' joinery, the tiller's iron, the cots, the lanterns)

deck.note: the deck flat across, its top the gun deck's less 7 ft 2 in all along (so it keeps her sheer: berth_deck.json deck), its planks 3 1/2 in (yellow pine, the 1795 section) laid as the gun deck's. It runs aft and forward to where the side's inside closes in to the middle line (the run aft, the bow forward), its ends over the orlop slice's framing (the berth deck's beams, ledges, deck transom and deck hook under the planks are slice 14's: berth_deck.json). The openings (openings) go down to the orlop; the masts, the pumps' trees and the cable scuttles pass through holes; the capstan's spindle and the bitts' posts stand on it

planking.note: yellow pine plank 3 1/2 in thick (1795 section), 7 in wide, laid as the gun deck's, its butts and plugs on its beams under it (the orlop slice's, at the gun deck's stations: berth_deck.json beams). Drawn by the material from the 'Planking' and 'Margin' UVs (build_frigate.py's BerthDeckPlanks)

waterway.note: the waterway's cove along the deck's edge as the gun deck's (gundeck_1797.json deck.waterway), the waterway timber's top flush with the planks for 10 in in from the side (the 'Margin' UV); it stops where the side closes in to 0.4 m (estimate)

side.note: the side's inside between the decks: the ceiling (the inner planking over the frames), the skin's inner face (skin.py's GUN surface, 16 in in from the moulded surface along its normal: the gun deck's GunWall) carried down from the gun deck's planks to the berth deck's waterway, along the whole deck and round the run and the bow to the middle line. Aft of the wardroom the stern's knuckle (the wing transom, skin.KNUCKLE: the run below closing in to the sternpost, the counter above it out to the full breadth) steps the ceiling out: a flat across between the two, the wing transom's top ceiled over (estimate). The rudder's head rises abaft the deck's after end at this height: no helm port on this deck. Painted as the gun deck's side (Interior)

overhead.note: the gun deck's framing seen from the berth deck (berth_deck.json gun_deck_beams): its planks 4 in thick on beams 18 in sided and 15 in moulded (the 1795 section's '15 x 18') at every other station of the spar deck's and gun deck's beam stations (0.8312 m apart: the stanchions on the three decks stand over one another), with a ledge (6 by 5 in) between each two; no waist on this deck, so they run the whole length. Where a member would cross an opening in the gun deck (a hatchway's coaming, the skylight, the scuttle, a mast, the capstan's barrel, the bitts' posts, the cable scuttles) it is cut: half beams from the side to a carling either side (8 by 8 in), head ledges across between them at the opening's ends. The beams' ends rest on a clamp along the side (12 in deep, 6 in thick: the gun deck's clamp carries the guns' weight), each held by a hanging knee under it (9 in sided, arms 36 in) and a lodging knee in the angle with the side forward of the wardroom; a turned stanchion (7 in) under every beam on the middle line where the room allows. Aft of the wardroom, where the side steps in under the knuckle, the hanging knees' upright arms have no side to lie on: none there (all estimate, period practice for a frigate's lower deck)
overhead.berth_framing_note: the berth deck's own beams, ledges and carlings under its planks, which the orlop slice builds (berth_deck.json beams, ledges, carlings): 16 in sided (estimate) and 14 in moulded (the 1795 section), ledges and carlings as the gun deck's

knee.note: a hanging knee under each beam end where the side under it is fair (the step at the knuckle less than least_side_step_m within the knee's arm)

lodging_knee.note: as the gun deck's (gundeck_1797.json overhead.lodging_knee) at the gun deck's beams forward of the wardroom's fore bulkhead (in the wardroom the state rooms' joinery is in their bays; in the tiller room the bays are left for the tiller ropes' blocks, which wait on where the tiller goes): estimate

overhead.bay_note: the most a bulkhead or partition (wardroom, steerage, officers_rooms, sick_bay x_m) may move from its card x to stand in a bay between the beams, head ledges and knees overhead (berthdeck.py bay_x): more fails the build, the card giving each its x in a bay
overhead.stanchion_note: a stanchion under each gun deck beam on the middle line, forward of the wardroom's fore bulkhead and in the wardroom clear of its table, where nothing stands within stanchion_clear_m of it (the gun deck's ladders' feet, the openings, the masts, the pumps, the capstan's step, the bitts)

openings.note: the openings through the berth deck down to the orlop (berth_deck.json openings: the gun deck's SpiritHatch, MainHatch and ForeHatchFore go on down one under the other, ForeHatchFore a little shorter at its after end; AfterLadderway the berth deck's own, to starboard of the gun deck after ladder's foot). Each with a coaming 6 in high and 3 in thick; a grating over the spirit room's and the main hatch (as the gun deck's, its edges in a rabbet half an inch into the coaming), the ladderways open with a ladder down. The gun deck's AfterHatch and ForeHatch (its ladders land on these planks), its wardroom skylight and the fore scuttle stop at this deck

items.name: AfterLadderway
items.note: the berth deck's own ladderway down to the orlop's cockpit: to starboard of the gun deck after ladder's foot, between two of the berth deck's beams (its coamings on them: the ledge between is cut, with carlings along its sides), under the gun deck's after hatch's starboard edge

items.name: ForeHatchFore
items.note: under the gun deck's ForeHatchFore grating, its after end a little short of the gun deck's (inside_x_m) so its coaming stands clear of the room at the gun deck fore ladder's foot; the ladder down to the orlop hangs in it

openings.wells_note: no wells: under each opening the orlop slice's (14) overhead and platforms show (the cable scuttles keep their lead lining down scuttle_well_ft, as far as the gun deck leads the cable). A ladder down lands on the orlop's top: an orlop platform's level where one stands under its foot (orlop.py platform_levels: the platforms are laid level fore and aft), else orlop_below_in under this deck's top (keeping her sheer)

ladders.note: a ladder down each ladderway to the orlop, hung from the inside face of its coaming, 62 degrees as the gun deck's, its foot on the orlop's top (an orlop platform's level, else openings orlop_below_in: berth_deck.json ladders_down); the gun deck's ladders land on this deck: nothing stands within clear_m beyond their feet

through.note: what comes down through the gun deck onto or through this one (berth_deck.json ending_on_the_berth_deck): the double capstan's spindle from the gun deck capstan's barrel to its step on these planks, the step an oak block bolted through to the beam and ledge under it (the orlop slice's); the riding bitts' posts on down to these planks, let into them; the pumps' trees (the chain pumps' four square pipes, the brake pumps' two bored trees) on down through holes to the planks' underside, below which they are the orlop slice's; the masts through holes wedged as the gun deck's; the cables down their scuttles (lead collars) to the tiers below. Sizes estimate

tiller.note: not built in this slice: the counter closes round the rudder head only at the gun deck's height, so this deck does not reach it, and where the tiller goes (hung under the quarterdeck's beams in the great cabin, the lower stern reshaped so it sits here as on Constitution, or none) is still to be decided. As drawn for this deck: the iron tiller (museum_1812: an iron tiller on the berth deck aft of the wardroom) in the rudder head's mortise in the slot between the wing transom's ceiled top and the gun deck's beams, led forward just under the beams (gap_under_beams_in) along her sheer to its end over the tiller room, square to the middle line with the helm amidships; the tiller ropes from the wheel come down through the gun deck in lead bushes (deck.py tiller_legs) through lead-lined holes in the gun deck's members, round a sheave block under each (hung from the member's side) and out to a block at the side abaft them (side_blocks_x_m, side_block_in from the ceiling), then in to an iron eye at the tiller's end. Hard over the end swings hard_over_deg either way, clear of the side and the bulkhead (checked). Iron forged square tapering to the end (sizes estimate, period practice: a 44's tiller about 18 ft long)
tiller.rudder_axis_note: the rudder turns about its pintles' line (skin.py's rudder); the tiller swings about that line's point at the tiller's height

wardroom.note: the wardroom (profile_1849: the officers' mess abaft the steerage, state rooms either side): across the ship from its after bulkhead (forward of the tiller ropes' legs and the hanging knee under the gun deck beam at -21.73) to its fore bulkhead; four state rooms a side, about 6 ft 2 in long (1.76 to 1.96 m as their partitions stand in the bays between the beams overhead), their inboard walls fore and aft wall_y_m out from the middle line with a door into the wardroom, partitions between them clear of the hanging knees. The mizzen comes down through the wardroom; its long table stands under the skylight (the gun deck's WardroomSkylight) with chairs round it, its lantern on a bar between the skylight's carlings. Deal joinery painted (Interior); all sizes estimate

steerage.note: the steerage (profile_1849): across the ship forward of the wardroom, the spirit room's hatch in it, closed forward by a bulkhead with a door either side of the middle line (the capstan's spindle stands forward of it): the midshipmen's and mates' berth (estimate)

officers_rooms.note: three rooms along each side forward of the steerage, six in all (profile_1849: the rooms forward of the steerage; whose they were is an estimate: the surgeon's, the purser's and the master's, the other three store rooms): their inboard walls fore and aft wall_y_m out, partitions between them clear of the hanging knees, each with a door; the middle of the deck open between them (the after ladderway down to the cockpit, the gun deck after ladder's foot, the capstan's step and the chain pumps)

sick_bay.note: the sick bay forward (profile_1849; in the 1800s frigates' sick bays were forward on the berth deck under the forecastle, where the air was best): across the ship between its after bulkhead and its fore bulkhead abaft the fore mast, the riding bitts' posts through it; hanging cots along each side for the sick (a canvas bed in a wooden frame, slung from the beams: cots_a_side rows a side, the outer row inboard of the hanging knees' heads so its clews' hooks clear the knees), a dispensary chest. Sizes estimate

berthing.note: the crew's hammocks slung at night (pose collection BerthDeck_Hammocks: by day they were lashed up in the nettings) fore and aft between hooks under the gun deck's beams two beams apart (hook_span_beams: the stores kit's hammock at that span), each hook beside its beam's hanging knee (so the outer rows hang out under the knees' arms), 14 in a man across (spacing_in: the US Navy's allowance) with heads and tails staggered (alternate rows on the beams between), over the crew's deck from the officers' rooms' fore wall to the sick bay's after bulkhead as built (from_x_m and to_x_m, when not null, cut it shorter) and, in the rows that pass inboard of the officers' rooms' walls, aft between them to the steerage's bulkhead; where the beams are whole over the row (not cut for an opening above), the body clear_m under the knees of the beams it passes and side_clear_m in from the clamp and the ceiling, and clear_m clear of the middle line's stanchions, the masts, the pumps, the ladders and the lanterns. Each hammock and hook a linked copy of the stores kit's (stores.py). The berth deck slings about 110 this way; the rest of a crew of about 450 would have slung theirs on the gun deck between the guns (estimate: not modelled in this slice)

messes.note: the crew's messes by day (pose collection BerthDeck_Messes): a mess table hung at the side under every other gun deck beam along the crew's deck (the stores kit's MessTable, hinged to a cleat on the side and slung from the beam over it), a bench either side, a mess kid on the table and a sea chest against the side between the messes (stores kit). A mess of eight a table (estimate)
messes.sling_note: the table's two slings run up to eyebolts under the beam over it this far either side of the beam's middle: inside the hammock hooks' plates beside the beam's knee (berthing), which come within about 4.9 in of it
messes.chest_note: the chest's back this far off the side over its height, and its foot a tenth of an inch clear of the waterway's cove (which stands out 3 in from the side along the deck), whichever keeps it further in

lanterns.note: horn lanterns as the gun deck's (gundeck_1797.json lanterns) but smaller (size), hung on a short hook in the gun deck planks' underside in the bays listed (x_m: the bay's middle nearest that x, within max_shift_m (half a station: each x_m is its bay's middle as built) and its own room, whose y_m across is under the planks, clear of the carlings, head ledges and the openings through the gun deck): the crew's deck's over the middle line, where the beams are cut for the openings above and no hammocks hang (a lantern among the hammocks was a fire risk), the two forward ones either side of the fore hatchways, one in the steerage, the tiller room, the sick bay (two) and the bow; the wardroom's over its table from a bar between the skylight's carlings, shadowed so it stops at its bulkheads. Each a light in the game data (berthdeck.json lights) in its zone: berth_deck, wardroom, sick_bay

size.note: the hung lanterns smaller than the gun deck's (body 7 in across and 9 in high, a 3 in roof) on a short hook (estimate: a small horn lantern below decks), so each one's dish hangs about level with the gun deck's beams' underside, the way a man walking the deck already stoops: whoever clears the beams clears the lanterns. The wardroom's, over its table, is the gun deck's size

light_budget.note: eleven lanterns and the wardroom's; the sick bay's, the steerage's (unshadowed, its reach would stop 0.81 m out at the wardroom's bulkhead: cast_shadows on its entry), the two forward crew's (unshadowed they would stop 3 m out at the sick bay's bulkhead, short of the fore messes) and the wardroom's cast shadows so they stop at their bulkheads, the rest are unshadowed with radius_m held short of the bulkheads between zones they would shine through (berthdeck.py lanterns). No light probes below in this slice

lanterns.zones_note: each light is in a zone (berth_deck, wardroom, sick_bay): in the game a light should light only the objects of its own zone (lighting channels: berthdeck.json below.zones), or, unshadowed, it shines through the planks onto the gun deck's guns and through the side onto the sea

handover.note: what build_frigate.py writes to berth_deck.json for the orlop slice (14), from this deck as built: these are its notes; its values are the deck's own (BerthDeck.handover)
handover.about: slice 13's hand-over to the orlop slice (14): the berth deck's line, its own beams' stations and sizes, and what passes through it, written by build_frigate.py from the berth deck as built. Metres in the ship's frame (x forward, y to starboard, z up; the origin on the middle line at midships on the load waterline, waterline A); sizes in inches where the name ends _in
handover.sources: the 1926 midship section (NARA, the orlop slice's reading): the berth deck's top 7 ft 2 in under the gun deck's top. The 1795 midship section drawn from Humphreys' specifications (NARA 75841360, measured at 4.0 px an inch from its keel's 18 by 24 in): lower deck plank to gun deck plank 6 ft 4 in on a gun deck 23 ft 3 in over the rabbet, the lower deck about 17 ft over it; our gun deck stands 7.37 m (24 ft 2 in) over the rabbet (the 1927 lines' port sills less 24 in), so 7 ft 2 in under it puts our berth deck 17 ft over the rabbet amidships, where the 1795 section has it (the 10 in more between our decks is our gun deck standing higher). Its beams: 14 in moulded (written '14 x 1?', the second figure unclear; 14 3/4 in drawn) and its planks 3 1/2 in yellow pine; the gun deck's beams '15 x 18' (15 in drawn deep), read as moulded by sided
handover.line_note: the deck's top (flat across), every 0.25 m: the gun deck's line less 7 ft 2 in, so it keeps her sheer. Underside of the planks: the top less plank_in
handover.ends_note: where the side's inside (the ceiling, 16 in in from the moulded surface) is 0.6 m out at the deck's top (deck.beams_end_half_breadth_m), as the gun deck's beams stop: aft the run closes in to the sternpost, forward the bow. half_breadth_inside_at_top_m is that inside at the deck's top, every 0.25 m
handover.beams_note: the berth deck's beams (the orlop's overhead, built by the orlop slice): at the spar deck's and gun deck's stations carried down (station_pitch_m apart), a beam every other station and a ledge between, so the stanchions on each deck stand over one another; down here the waist's stations are whole beams. Straight (no round up), their tops at the planks' underside. Cut where an opening below (openings) or a mast passes, the cut ends taken by carlings either side from the whole beam abaft to the one before it
handover.ledges_note: between the beams, as the gun deck's overhead has (the 1795 section draws ledges on the lower deck); their tops at the planks' underside
handover.openings_note: the openings through the berth deck (inside_m: the hole in the planks, [fore and aft, across], inside_x_m and inside_y_m its edges; with_coaming_m: with the berth deck's own coaming, 6 in high and 3 in thick as your orlop hatches'; y_m the middle's offset to starboard). The gun deck's SpiritHatch and MainHatch go on down one under the other at the gun deck's x and size, and ForeHatchFore a little shorter at its after end. The gun deck's AfterHatch and ForeHatch (its ladderways) stop at the berth deck: its planks run on under them, and the gun deck's ladders land there (gun_deck_ladders_land). The ladders down to the orlop are in AfterLadderway, the berth deck's own, and ForeHatchFore (ladders_down)
handover.stop_note: the gun deck's openings that end on the berth deck's planks: the wardroom's skylight lights the wardroom, the fore scuttle comes down onto it, and the gun deck's AfterHatch and ForeHatch, its ladderways, land their ladders on it (gun_deck_ladders_land): none goes further
handover.ladders_note: slice 13's ladders from the berth deck to the orlop, 62 degrees as the gun deck's, each hung from the inside face of a coaming (6 in up): aft from AfterLadderway's forward edge going aft into the cockpit, to starboard of the middle line (y_m); forward from ForeHatchFore's after edge going forward onto the fore platform. foot_x_m and foot_z_m are where the ladder's line meets the orlop's top (6 ft 4 in under the berth deck's top, keeping its sheer), drop_m its height from the coaming's top; foot_stringers_x_m where its stringers stand; keep_clear_m the room to keep clear round each foot (the stringers and a foot beyond, the ladder's width)
handover.gun_deck_ladders_note: the gun deck's ladder lands on the berth deck's planks here (slice 12); slice 13 keeps 0.3 m clear beyond its foot and leaves out the stanchion it would meet
handover.masts_note: each mast where it passes the berth deck: its axis and radius at the deck's top and at its own beams' underside (the axes as the rig has them; the fore and mizzen heels stand on your keelson steps, the axes unmoved). The hole in the planks is the mast's radius plus the gun deck's 0.5 in gap, wedged as the gun deck's
handover.pumps_note: the gun deck's pumps (gundeck_1797.json pumps): the chain pumps' case aft of the main mast on the middle line, the pair of brake pumps forward of it. Their tubes come straight down through the berth deck (tubes: each one's middle and half size, the chain pumps' square pipes and the brake pumps' round trees; slice 13 cuts the holes and builds them to its planks' underside); from there down to the well they are yours
handover.cable_scuttles_note: the cables' scuttles in the berth deck straight under the gun deck's (gundeck_1797.json bow), 20 in round with lead collars, one each side of the middle line: the cables come down through both to your tiers
handover.gun_deck_beams_note: the berth deck's overhead (slice 13 builds it): the gun deck's beams under its 4 in planks at the same stations, a ledge between; underside is their underside every 0.25 m
ending_on_the_berth_deck: the capstan's spindle comes down through the gun deck to its step on the berth deck's planks, bolted through to a beam (slice 13): nothing below
the riding bitts' posts come down through the gun deck to the berth deck and are let into its planks (slice 13): nothing below them
the berth deck's cabins and partitions (slice 13) stand on its planks
the gun deck's after and fore ladders land on the berth deck's planks (slice 12 as built), so under them the berth deck is planked and the beams and ledges run on whole (gun_deck_ladders_land)
handover.who_builds_what: the boundary is the underside of the berth deck's planks: below it the orlop slice (the berth deck's beams, ledges, carlings, hanging and lodging knees, the clamp under the beams' ends, the ceiling up to the planks, the pillars on the orlop under the beams); above it slice 13 (the planks, waterways, the side's ceiling up to the gun deck, the gun deck's beams, ledges, carlings, knees, chocks and clamp overhead, the stanchions on the berth deck, coamings, ladders down to the orlop, the pumps' tubes to the planks' underside, cabins and fittings)

budget_note: the plan's figure for slice 13 (the berth deck, loaded only when below, streamed: build.json berthdeck.triangles_below): a starting point, not a ceiling (Bean, Nov 12: frame rate is the only hard limit); the hammocks and the messes are counted apart as linked copies (berthdeck.triangles_copies)

meets.note: the berth deck's parts that meet another part of the ship (or each other) by design, each pair with why and how far (in) either may go into the other; every other meeting fails the build (build_frigate's berthdeck_room, deck.room). Each entry: the parts on one side, the parts on the other, why, the depth allowed (measured, plus a quarter inch, rounded up to a twentieth). A designed contact the build no longer finds fails it too
